computational_result.title: Numerical integration of the A=2.4 isothermal-sphere collapse solution
computational_result.description: A partial numerical reproduction and cross-check of the similarity solution described by Shu (1977), focused here on agreement between higher-order Taylor-series integration and adaptive RK45 for the dimensionless enclosed mass at x=0.001.
computational_result.research_question: Do the Taylor-series and RK45 implementations produce endpoint masses agreeing within the test's configured absolute tolerance for A=2.4?
computational_result.scientific_field: Astrophysical fluid dynamics; self-similar gravitational collapse
computational_result.status_rationale: The automated Taylor-versus-RK45 endpoint-mass test passes. This is a numerical cross-check, not a complete reproduction or independent validation of the governing equations, assumptions, or the paper's full results.

numerical_targets.title: Endpoint dimensionless enclosed mass at x=0.001
numerical_targets.description: Agreement of the Taylor-series and RK45 computed values of m(x) at the common integration endpoint.
numerical_targets.scope: A=2.4; inward integration from x=10 to x=0.001 using the documented asymptotic initial conditions.
numerical_targets.notes: Taylor result 1.8852400343916835; RK45 result 1.8852400344047633; absolute difference 1.3079759497713894e-11; configured allowed absolute difference 1e-8; automated test status pass. The tolerance is documented, but when it was established relative to the comparison has not been independently recorded. These are endpoint masses, not extrapolated central mass m0 values.

limitations: This record covers only the Taylor-versus-RK45 endpoint-mass comparison for A=2.4 at x=0.001.
The two methods share the governing similarity equations, asymptotic initial conditions, and endpoint mass definition; their agreement is not a fully independent mathematical verification.
The comparison does not compare extrapolated central mass m0 values between Taylor and RK45.
The published Table 1 value m0=1.88 is rounded and is not a high-precision benchmark for the endpoint mass target; it is therefore not attached as a reference dataset to NT-001.
The exact code revision associated with the archived numerical output has not been confirmed.
The reproducibility guide records GNU Octave 10.3.0 for the test, but the operating system and exact execution timestamp are not established in the available output record.
No formal independent scientific assessment has been recorded.
The RK4-versus-RK45 central-mass and profile comparisons, and the exploratory spectral calculations, are not included as targets in this first minimal v2 example.
